facts.raw_span: skin fragility since early infancy
Symptoms improved in winter and worsened in summer
Mild xerosis with superficial skin erosions
Erythematous residual macules from previous erosions
Some lesions had unusual linear geographic contour
Lesions predominantly located at areas of friction
No history of blistering
Serological markers for celiac disease were negative
Complete separation of the stratum corneum
Clean split just above the stratum granulosum
2 heterozygous mutations in exon 2 of the CDSN gene
Normal results for: Collagen IV and VII, α6 and β4 integrines, Laminine-332

support_spans: skin fragility since early infancy
Mild xerosis with superficial skin erosions
Complete separation of the stratum corneum

concepts.why: The patient's skin fragility, xerosis, and superficial skin erosions, along with the complete separation of the stratum corneum and mutations in the CDSN gene, support the diagnosis of Peeling skin syndrome.

support_spans: Symptoms improved in winter and worsened in summer
Lesions predominantly located at areas of friction
contradict_spans: 2 heterozygous mutations in exon 2 of the CDSN gene
concepts.why: The patient's symptoms improving in winter and worsening in summer, along with lesions located at areas of friction, support the diagnosis of Keratolytic winter erythema.
It explains the unusual linear geographic contour of some lesions and the clean split just above the stratum granulosum.
It explains the negative serological markers for celiac disease and the normal results for collagen IV and VII, α6 and β4 integrines, and laminine-332.

rationales.F01: Skin fragility is a key feature of peeling skin syndrome.
rationales.F02: Seasonal variation in symptoms is more typical of keratolytic winter erythema.
rationales.F05: Unusual linear geographic contour of lesions is characteristic of peeling skin syndrome.
rationales.F09: Complete separation of the stratum corneum is a distinctive histopathological feature of peeling skin syndrome.
rationales.F10: Clean split just above the stratum granulosum is a characteristic histopathological feature of peeling skin syndrome.
rationales.F11: Mutations in the CDSN gene are associated with peeling skin syndrome.

frontier_selector.why: The presence of 2 heterozygous mutations in exon 2 of the CDSN gene and specific skin biopsy findings such as complete separation of the stratum corneum decided it.
